utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember it properly, that was between 8.00 and 11.00. I think that the curfew was lifted at 8.00 in the morning. That's when the citizens could go out and tend to their various businesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you said that it applied to all citizens, what did you mean?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said that, I meant all generations, both genders, all ethnic groups. The only people who were exempted from that were officials from the police or the military or ambulance services. They were the only ones to whom the curfew did not apply.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Adjudicated Fact 1268.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, mentioning adjudicated fact, and being impossible to have all adjudicated facts in our heads, would it be a problem for you to add, Well, this is a challenge to the adjudicated fact? Or is it, when you mention an adjudicated fact, is it, by definition, a challenge?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is a challenge to adjudicated fact. Your Honours, if you want me to, I can read the adjudicated fact into the record, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: No, no. It's just to make sure that this is a challenge. It's not just a reference to an adjudicated fact; it is a challenge to the adjudicated fact?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's a challenge, yes. I thought that it was understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That's -- that's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, my understanding is that each and every one of the adjudicated facts is now being challenged, in total. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, concerning Doboj. We have the witness who --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. No, I understand that. I just want to know, Your Honours, because it has consequences for what we have to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, do you know where Dragalovci is in Doboj municipality?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a village on the regional road between Doboj and Prnjavor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What is its ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian ethnicity prevailed. There were also a few Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of any operation by the Serb forces which took place in that village on the 20th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of any operation and when it took place. However, as I was passing through the village, I did notice some traces of damage on the buildings there, probably as a result of some operation. But I don't know when the operation took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That village, Dragalovci, does it have a railway station?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is on the railroad which connects Doboj and Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Adjudicated Fact 1272.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you know of the existence of a hangar in the town of Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hangars, hangars? This is a very general term. I don't know what it could mean in Doboj, unless you are referring to military hangars.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any military hangars in the town of Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the southern part, in the area known as Usora neighbourhood, very close to the Bosanka factory that existed at the time. It was a fruit and vegetable processing factory, Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that those hangars, in mid-June 1992, were used for the accommodation of some individuals who had been arrested?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, for a while the military did keep detainees in those facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify, let's clarify. What place are we talking about? What hangar do you have in mind when you speak about hangars?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were military facilities or military hangars which used to house vehicles and personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What is the name of that part of town?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the entire area is known as Usora.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a camp in Bare at the beginning of July 1992 in Doboj municipality?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were military facilities in Bare as well. As far as I know, there were sub-ground -- or underground and ground depots for equipment. I was never there, but I know that there were some military facilities there. I believe that even to this day the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina use those facilities as military facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read a number of geographical terms --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, as to your previous question, you ask about a camp and the witness answered about military --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- facilities. Was that what you meant with your question when you asked for a camp?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if it was recorded, but the witness said that there was a -- that he knows there was a military facility, but was never there. So, therefore, I didn't see any point in pursuing any more, because obviously he wasn't aware of the fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The fact that he wasn't there does not necessarily mean that he wasn't aware. So if you mean -- if, by asking for a camp, you meant something else than a military facility, I would like you to clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I appreciate Your Honour's suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, did you ever hear -- do you know that there was a camp in Bare, a detention camp or a collection centre, from sometime in July to mid-August 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure when I heard that, but I did hear rumours about prisoners of war being detained as they were in Usora.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In those military --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in those military facilities in Bare.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: With regard to collection centres, do you know that in 1992 there was a collection centre where Muslim and Croat civilians were kept in the 4th of July Barracks, in a place called Miljkovac.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of the barracks in Doboj was the 4th of July, but I really don't know that civilians were ever kept there, I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a collection centre where Muslim and Croat civilians were kept in 1992, in Doboj municipality, and that camp was known as Seslija camp?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the name doesn't ring a bell. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Seslija Camp is at all?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just told you that I don't even know that there was a camp of that kind. Seslija is a crossroads. Actually, it is a place on the road between Doboj and, further on, Samac and Brod. And at S eslija, the road forks off to the right, and there it leads to Samac. And if you go on straight, you get to Brod. I'm not aware of any military facilities that ever existed there. I'm not aware of any camps having being set up there. I really don't know. I've never heard that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the railway station was used for the same purpose?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I've never heard that before. I've never heard the railway station being mentioned as used for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that something that was known as the SRC Ozren was used for the same purpose, i.e., as a collection centre for Muslim and Croat civilians?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SRC Ozren, in our language the "SRC" could stand for Sports and Recreation Centre, but I didn't know that such a centre ever existed in Ozren at the time. Therefore, I really don't know that people were ever kept at such a place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the secondary school was also used for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The secondary school, who bore the name of Djuro Pucar, was the place where refugees were billeted. And now, whether I have time, maybe it would be of some interest for me to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just briefly.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In very brief outline: Sometime in November 1992, a journalist came to visit me from Munich, Germany, the TV house Zoller and the journalist's name was Martin Rettmayer [phoen], and he asked me the same question you have just asked me now. He asked me about that locality, and some others, and said that those were camps, as far as he knew. And we went and checked those places. And I know that at the time I spoke to either the president or the secretary of the Red Cross, and he brought us the lists of those people who had spent some time in the secondary school. There were refugees from various regions, of different ethnicities. And later on, that journalist published a book about what he had learned, and he sent me that book from Germany. It has been translated. In the book, he described what he found on the site visit, as opposed to what he had heard before he came to Bosnia. In other words, there was nothing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the factory of tyres in Bare was also used as a collection centre?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never heard that before. I apologise for laughing, but I assure you that there has never been a tyre factory in Doboj. There never was and there isn't now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the mine in Stanari was also used as a collection centre?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I absolutely don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the primary school in Stanari?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The handball pitch?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear that. That is, indeed, a stadium where all sorts of tournaments, international, national, are held every year. But I've never heard that prisoners were ever kept there, that the place was used as a camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And something that is known as either Bosanska or perhaps Bosanka?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that was called Bosanska in Doboj was Bosanska Street, and I've never heard of Bosanka. That may be a mistake. Somebody may have put it in the context of those hangars, and also because the two are close, but I've never heard of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What about electricity poles factory in Rudanka?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is such a factory there. But I've never heard of it being used for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The village of Kotorsko?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know where it is. It is to the north, towards Derventa. I don't know of any collection centre or camp being there. I simply never heard of anything of that sort. It was actually a stronghold where there were armed formations placed during the Corridor Operation. A unit that was deployed there was from the so-called Handzar Division, a famous unit, but I don't know of any camps in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The "Piperi" shop?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know even what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of such a shop?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of the elementary school in the village of Grapska, used for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is such a village, but I never heard of the school there being used to that end.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Podnovlje?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Podnovlje is next to the main road that goes to Modrica and Samac. There was a school there where an army command was housed for a while, but I don't know of any camps there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And, lastly, a military barracks at Sevarlije?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Sevarlije is located to the south of Doboj, on the right bank of the Bosna River. There were certain military facilities and warehouses there, but I don't know of their use for any detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What about Putnikovo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Putnikovo Brdo also had military facilities. There was a firing range there, with a number of buildings, but I don't know of it being used for any prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was there a separation line at Putnikovo Brdo or was there any combat there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the lines were established there. And later on there was combat. I know of the 12th of July, for example, when the Muslim forces attempted an attack towards Doboj. There was fierce fighting there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For ease of reference, it is Adjudicated Fact 1279. I'm looking at the clock, Your Honours. Is it a good time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. We would take the break now and resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just before the witness comes back in again, I've informed Mr. Zecevic I'm going to raise it: Your Honours have heard for the last hour or so, effectively, every single adjudicated fact being challenged through this witness. Your Honours, I simply wish to observe this: As I've already remarked, that doesn't even remotely occur in the 65 ter summary that we got about this witness. The closest I suppose you could say it is that he will describe the situation in CSB Doboj and the SJBs in the territory after the outbreak of hostilities. Your Honours, I'm simply raising it at this time. There's nothing we can do about it. But for future reference, because we don't have statements from these witnesses, other than our interviews, which didn't deal with this at all, on the basis the Defence don't have statements, we would ask that we get proper 65 ter summaries which outline the specific issues that the witness will deal with, not in a general way, as put here. And if matters come to light after proofing has taken place, well, then we should be given an amended 65 ter summary so that we have some advance notice of the evidence that the witness is going to give.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, do you have a response to what Ms. Korner has just said?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It is entirely my fault; I agree. The point of the matter is the following: The issue of these adjudicated facts concerning Doboj came out only when the witness arrived over here, so after we filed our 65 ter -- our 65 ter submission. And we discussed it during the proofing. And I entirely accept I failed to put the Office of the Prosecutor on notice that this was discussed during the proofing of this witness. And I will keep that in mind, to inform the Office of the Prosecutor and the Trial Chamber of the events that -- or the issues that pop up during the proofing of the witnesses. However, I don't think that the office -- I mean, considering, in this case, I don't think that the Office of the Prosecutor would be prejudiced, because the cross-examination will be postponed after ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that is the point, of course. I accept - and that's why I'm not taking any point on this - because of postponement. But in normal circumstances, we would be going straight into cross-examination and we would have no idea at all that this was something we would have to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Zecevic, basically you do agree that it would be good practice to mention this in the witness summary?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, by all means, Your Honours, I accept that it's entirely my fault. I just -- I just failed -- forgot to prepare the proofing note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I must add that I'm relieved that you agree with Ms. Korner that this is the correct approach.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, please look at 16D1, tab 59A. Sir, it is a letter of the Ministry of the Interior from July 1992 to the security services centres, signed by Minister of the Interior Mico Stanisic. We see a signature there as well as a stamp. Please comment: Did you receive this document; and what it pertained to.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was an invitation to a collegium meeting that was to take place on the 11th of July, 1992. We received this notification, and I attended. It was the first collegium meeting since the outbreak of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D476, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you attend the collegium meeting on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. I can tell you that I was happy to see this notification. I prepared for the meeting because I was supposed to brief on the situation in the field. I thought about the situation, because a number of times before that I was toying with the idea of leaving the service. Having received this notification, I decided to attend to see what the situation will be like at the meeting, to see what the position is of the minister and the entire collegium, upon which I wanted to decide whether to stay with the MUP or leave and join the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Where did the collegium meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Belgrade, in Villa Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it all looked like, how many days it lasted, and what did you discuss?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, it took place in Belgrade, in Villa Bosanka. It began on the 11th. And we had a thorough discussion preceded by Minister Stanisic's opening remarks. We all participated and presented our respective problems in the areas we came from. Following that discussion, certain guide-lines were provided and conclusions adopted. The next day, on the 12th of July, we could address specific issues with the Public Security assistant to the minister, as well as the State Security assistant to the minister. So that day was the working day, if I may say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Mico Stanisic before the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we met once in the ministry building, the Ministry of the Interior, that is, in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in Sarajevo. We also met at a collegium meeting on the 11th of February in Banja Luka. Before that time, we were not closely acquainted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please look at tab 66, which is P160. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a document of the minister of the interior of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, brief analysis of functioning of the MUP so far and the outlines of its future activities. In brackets, "(Summary of the meeting of the MUP officials of 11th of July, 1992)." It says that it was drafted in Sarajevo in July 1992. Have you had occasion to see this document before?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since it is, of course, a summary, overview, of what was discussed and who said what, does it, in general terms, reflect what was, indeed, said at the meeting, as well as is it accurate as to who attended it and what problems were addressed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 9 in the Serbian, which is marked as page 6 - it is 9 in e-court - we see your name and title, head of the Doboj CSB. Can you comment on this part, briefly?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This reflects my contribution to the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the sake of the Trial Chamber, I wanted to say that the text spills over on the next page and the page following that; that is to say, pages 10 and 11 in e-court are also included.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I opened up my presentation by describing the sequence of events with the area of the centre and how parts of municipalities and public security stations were under occupation. It is accurately reflected in this document. I also spoke about the participation of the police in military operations and its consequences in the number of those killed and wounded who were from the police. Next, I discussed the problems which I believed were the most important and of which I wanted to acquaint Mr. Stanisic, as well as other associates of his. And I wanted to receive answers to the problems I presented. My decision whether to stay depended very much on my impression of whether I could continue working in such a way. I did mention that for any further participation of the police force in combat activities presents a problem. Perhaps I need not go into each and every sentence. In any case, I pointed out the problems of public security station buildings having been destroyed and that we were lacking personnel, as well as we were poorly equipped. I also pointed out the problem of financing, because the crisis staffs provided funds for the police to the extent possible, which then had an impact on being dependent on those financing the police. That is to say, those crisis staffs influenced the work of the police. Certain chiefs, for example, were appointed by the war staffs in question -- crisis staffs in question. I also mentioned that there was too much intrusion on part of local politicians into the work of the police, which greatly influenced the professional conduct of policemen. Local politics had a significant bearing on the work of the police and it was exercised through station chiefs and other managing personnel. Next, I pointed out the problems surrounding the Public Security Station in Doboj, where members of the army and paramilitary formations arrested people, bringing them into the police station, without any legal basis, first and foremost, and then without any proof or evidence that they should be deprived of liberty and treated in such way. Any opposition to that practice met with strong reaction. I told you earlier that people drew out weapons and that I, too, was threatened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, Mr. Bjelosevic, at the end of this meeting that was held on the 11th and 12th of July, certain conclusions were made - we can see them on page 23; in e-court, it is marked as page 20 - do you remember that these conclusions were reached then?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, these conclusions, were they reached on the basis of the consent, if I can put it that way, of the members of the collegium who were there, who were present in Belgrade on the 11th and 12th of July and on the basis of agreed positions, that is to say, as you had agreed at the meeting? Was that the case, or were these conclusions imposed in some other way?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's exactly the way it says here. On the basis of the discussion, proposals, suggestions, and on the basis of the introductory remarks made by the minister, where he provided certain guide-lines as to what was expected of the MUP. And these conclusions mentioned here were derived from that. It can also be said that these conclusions -- actually, that's not written here, but they have the nature of an operative plan, because you see that there are dead-lines that are set there and also who it should be carried out by. So this document is one that truly encouraged me. I have to say that again. These conclusions encouraged me, the minister's position encouraged me, because he said that all the problems that were registered at the meeting, and that did not only depend on the minister and the ministry, would be dealt with by a cabinet meeting, that he would discuss it with the prime minister and other ministers in charge of various fields involved. He said that he would ask the appropriate authorities to have certain things discussed and agreed upon with the Main Staff, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After the meeting -- what were your thoughts after the meeting? Since you told us about your thoughts before the meeting, now tell us, finally, how you had experienced the meeting.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I experienced it as a very constructive meeting. I understood the minister to be a man who was seriously committed to the strengthening of the institution and its further developments and its functioning on the basis of the Constitution and law. This is something that he repeated several times as he made his introductory remarks and took part in the discussion. It was pointed out that regardless of all the complexity involved, as was ultimately proven, he insisted on people acting in accordance with the law to a maximum degree and that the safety of the property of all citizens be ensured, also that certain crimes -- or, rather, all crimes that were committed should be uncovered and the perpetrators should be prosecuted. He repeated that, saying, Irrespective of ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After this meeting, did you remain a member of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As soon as I came back, I spoke to the persons who I wanted to head departments within the CSB, persons I had spoken to earlier on as well. I invited them to come in, and I told them about the meeting, itself, on the basis of my own notes, because we didn't have any other documents at that point. I told them what the position of the collegium was, and then we started establishing the department as envisaged by law. The heads of various offices were appointed, and we started establishing all the elements that a security services centre should have. And all of this started functioning according to the different lines of work. Immediately after that, I called in the different station chiefs and I familiarised them with the same content that I told the future heads of department about. From then onwards, in the CSB we established certain records that are supposed to be kept when these departments are operational. Also, we started with instructive supervision from the centre in respect of individual stations. As for the situation as it was in different stations, we, as a team, discussed all of that and informed the MUP about what the situation was and provided instructions to the stations on the ground in terms of how they should improve things. Immediately after this collegium, somehow the financing started as well. The MUP started financing this along the chain. Money started coming in, and this was an important element on the basis of which subordinates could be required to be loyal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am going to show you document 1D63. That is tab 69. This is a document of the Ministry of the Interior. This was communicated a few days after the collegium. The date is the 19th of July, 1992. This was submitted to all centres of security services in the territory of the MUP of Republika Srpska, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it has to do with instructions. And there is the RZ questionnaire pertaining to war crimes that is attached. Do you remember receiving this document, and do you remember acting in accordance with this instruction and this form?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This followed after the meeting that we discussed. I know that we received this dispatch and this questionnaire, and they were acted upon. Truth to tell, the communications system was not fully operational, but as soon as possible, this was dealt with. But I do remember this letter, specifically, and I know that this questionnaire, this form, was filled out and sent on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I really don't want to become boring about this, but these are important matters, Your Honour, and they should be dealt with, because it devalues the evidence, as far as Mr. Zecevic is concerned, if it is all didn't by leading questions. "Do you remember receiving this document," and "Do you remember acting in accordance with this instruction and this form," all of that is leading. The proper question should be: Did you receive the document; what did you do about it? Particularly in the light of his assertion that at an earlier stage he never received any documents at all from Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Again, I'm sorry. You were right, Ms. Korner, to a certain extent, I should say. I will try my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, let us look at the next document, 1D76. That is tab 224.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just try to find it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 224, you said?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I seem to have a problem with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You can see it on the monitor if you cannot find it in the binder.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying, but I cannot find it under that number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you assist him, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please show this to the Office of the Prosecutor and then provide the document. [Interpretation] Here's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Bjelosevic, did you receive this document from the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Let us see what the next question is. What did you do in respect of that document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we acted in accordance with it. We did what was requested here. We provided all the information we had available at that point in time, and we submitted that to the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document, in your view, can it be linked to the conclusions of the collegium or not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. It is derived from those conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What is the date on this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is the 19th of July, 1992. Of course, at the end I recognised Minister Stanisic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this document and the previous document, did you inform the chiefs of public security stations in your area about the content of those documents?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. There was no other way of collecting the data involved. We had to do it through the public security stations, because every station had records in its own area and they were responsible for the area that they covered. After receiving this dispatch, this was forwarded to the stations. And then at the level of the centre, all of this information was brought together and then sent on to the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Document 201, D201, tab 70, could we please have that shown.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 20th of July, 1992. It says "Security Services Centre," and then there is your name at the bottom of the page and your position, and then there's a signature and stamp, and then the president of the War Presidency, name, signature, stamp. Can you tell us what this is all about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a request for deployment in the MUP. I have already told you that after the meeting in Belgrade, I embarked upon the establishment and replenishment of the CSB Doboj. This is a request for Mr. Mirko Stojcinovic to be freed from the military, because he was in the Vucijak Brigade, and be appointed chief of the Public Security Sector. As you can see, this was still being co-ordinated with the local organs of government. The president of the War Presidency, Mr. Paravac, also agreed with this personnel appointment, and he confirms this request by his own signature and stamp. Let me note that after a certain procedure that was followed, Mr. Stojcinovic was, indeed, appointed to that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D477, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The next document is 207D1, tab 85.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a letter of mine that I, as chief of the Security Services Centre, sent to the Command of the Doboj Operations Group. After the procedure was carried through for Mr. Stojcinovic's appointment as chief of the Public Security Sector, this was sent to the command, and then the command met our request.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So after that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command relieved him of the duty that he held in the army up until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was this gentleman truly appointed chief of that sector?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, we sent a copy to the command once we received the appointment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The following document is 1D58, tab 71.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Do you want to tender the last one?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, if there is no opposition, I --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic says "if there is no opposition." I'm merely asking if he wishes to tender it. I haven't objected so far. I've only asked for information about the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D478, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is an order by the ministry. Did you receive it at the CSB Doboj? Are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We received it and then we forwarded it to our public security stations with our accompanying letter. The police department was tasked with monitoring the implementation of the minister's order. In other words, we acted upon this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The following document I would like to show you -- or, rather, the date of this document is 23rd July; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The following document is 1D59, tab 72. Mr. Bjelosevic, did you receive this document from the Ministry of the Interior? Do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the document. We also proceeded in accordance with this document. However, we had a problem in the field, as I have already explained in my previous answers. I said that we had public security stations that had been torched or destroyed and that in some places our registers had been destroyed. However, we did act upon this order by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain. How did you act upon this order? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the employees, and especially the reserve forces, because we already knew the status of those who were our staff members and they had already been vetted, so the reserve forces and the newly-appointed personnel were vetted, especially in those stations where the registers were preserved. And if we established that an individual had a criminal record, they would be removed from our war deployment schedule. In places where our records were destroyed, we tried to work through police officers who were sector leaders because they knew people by name. Every sector leader knew almost the entire population in their respective areas. And wherever possible and whenever possible, we tried to have them help us in establishing whether an individual had a criminal record, whether they were prone to crime, whether they had ever been engaged in the disruption of public law and order, but still we acted upon the minister's orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And what about those people against whom proceedings were being conducted at that very moment; what did you do with them?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were also removed from the wartime deployment schedule if proceedings were being conducted against them at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If any such individual against whom criminal proceedings were being conducted at that moment and if such an individual was a member of the Ministry of the Interior and if that person was in custody at that moment, what would happen?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a person was in custody, he could not have been on duty. So if they were not physically on duty, if they were not physically in service, they would be removed from the deployment schedule, because that would just increase our numbers and the strength would not reflect the numbers on paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And let me just tell you that public security stations were duty-bound to implement the order in their respective territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you now look at document P590, tab 74. Sir, are you familiar with this letter?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That letter was sent from the Doboj Security Services Centre. It was drafted based on an order, an order by the minister. The information was drafted by the Security Services Centre, I signed it, and it was sent to the ministry. You can see a link between a certain document that was issued on the 19th July, 1992. Let me just add to this that you can see, from the letter, what I have repeated on several occasions in this courtroom, namely, what the situation was like at that time; that chaos reigned, that there were groups of armed individuals, and so on and so forth. I don't want to go over the same grounds yet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say that there was a connection between a certain document which was either drafted or issued on the 19th of July, 1992, what document did you have in mind, precisely?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see its number. We have already commented upon that document that had arrived from the ministry. In other words, this information was drafted pursuant to the minister's order. I don't know if I've made myself clear when I tried to explain which document it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at 1D55, at tab 86. My question is this: Did you receive this document? If you did, did you act upon it? If so, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we received the document. And you can see a handwritten addition which says: "To the SJBs Doboj, Maglaj, Teslic, Derventa, Modrica, Bosanski Samac, and Petrovo." The minister issues an order reminding us that we had to act in compliance with the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And what is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 10th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let's look another document, 208D1, tab 88.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... could I just ask: Whose writing is that on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you go back to the previous document, Mr. Bjelosevic. Would you be able to recognise the handwriting at the bottom of the page? And there is also something at the top of the page also in handwriting.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Cyrillic handwriting, that is my handwriting, where it says: "Send to all SJBs." And at the bottom, I think that Mirko Blazanovic actually listed all the SJBs to whom the document had to be sent. He was on duty -- or, rather, he was the chief of the police department at the CSB, and this is his handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document that I asked for previously was 208D1, tab 88.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, the document was issued on the 12th of August, 1992, and it was sent to the public security stations and the National Security Service. Your name is on the document, and there is a signature as well. Do you remember this document? Is this your document? And what can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document bears the date that you have just mentioned, and I signed it, as the chief of centre. It was sent, as you can see, to the public security stations in the territory of the Security Services Centre in Doboj as well as to the National Security Service. This is an order, an order sent by the minister, forwarded by myself to the public security stations in my territory. This is Minister Stanisic's order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The text of the order that you forwarded to the SJBs, is it identical to the text of the order that you received from the ministry?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can actually see the quotation signs. And it says here that we received the order by fax. There were no teleprinter communications means at that moment. My introduction is: "We have received a fax with the following contents ..." And then I quote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I would like to tender the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D479, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The following document I would like to show you is 1D56, tab 93.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I have a problem. I don't have it. No, no, I have it. Sorry. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch from the ministry. Did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a repeat of the document. Something with similar contents had already been received, but this one was sent on the 17 of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The ministry repeated its document. Did you also do the same; did you repeat your instruction to the SJBs in your territory?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you acted upon this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bjelosevic, the Central Prison in Doboj, who was its warden, if you remember, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were two men. I don't know who -- I can't remember who the warden was and who his deputy was. Miroslav Vidic and Mirko Slavuljica were their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me just briefly show you P1304, at tab 237. Are you familiar with this document? Are you familiar with any of the facts in this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that -- or, rather, what I have just said is corroborated by this document and that is that the two of them were the two persons in charge of the district prison in Doboj. And as for the contents of the entire document, I've not seen that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bjelosevic, under whose competence functioned the Central Prison in Doboj throughout 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prisons, or correctional facilities, as they were called at the time, were under the competence of the Ministry of Justice, as is the case today. The Ministry of Justice is the body competent to regulate the work of those institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 1D176, tab 75.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Seventy-five?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, tab 75.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document? On page 2, you can see the signature block.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the document, and I recognise Minister Stanisic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is dated the 27th of July, 1992. Do you recall having received it in the CSB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What did you do with it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did precisely as I was asked to do, which was to clean up our own ranks. I hope the word won't be taken the wrong way. We had already initiated that activity. It didn't happen overnight. We were carrying out checks, and any surplus staff were put at the disposal of the departments of the Ministry of Defence. In parallel, we carried out training and further education of the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, if you can recall, when did you receive the document we saw containing those conclusions of the 11th of July, 1992? Can you remember, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot. I don't know when it came to Doboj. I do know that immediately upon my return, not waiting for the actual minutes to be published, and based on what had been agreed upon, we immediately set about implementing the collegium conclusions. At the time, we had pronounced problems in the functioning of the communications system, and the road between Doboj and Pale, where the seat was, was a complicated one. One had to take different roads at a time, and it was difficult to get through. So I can't tell you anything more precise than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If you recall, according to all the conclusions of the 11th of July collegium, did the minister of the interior receive any instructions?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. And later on, supervision was exercised by inspectors from the seat of the ministry over how those conclusions were implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did it happen that some of those documents containing instructions were repeated a number of times by the ministry?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We saw one such document a moment ago, because we see the words "I order" again. Before we received the minutes in its integral form, we had received segments, individual documents, by way of orders to implement specific measures relating to specific conclusions from the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but I think there may have been a problem in translation at page 75, line 1. Question: "If you recall," alledgedly we heard in English, "according to all the conclusions of the 11th of July, did the minister of the interior receive any instructions?" The answer didn't seem to bear any relation to that, but I'm wondering if that was a correct translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: It should have been "Ministry of the Interior."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is, indeed, the wrong interpretation -- wrong -- I was recorded wrong. I said "sent from the ministry," Did the minister of interior send any instructions concerning in relation to the decisions of the collegium of the 11th? Your Honours, I think it's the appropriate time, because I'm about to move to another topic, so thank you. Thank you, Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And so we take the adjournment for the week, and we resume -- I believe we're back in Courtroom I on Monday morning at 9.00. Mr. Bjelosevic, I would remind you of the caution that I gave you at the adjournment the first day; that you aren't to discuss the case with anyone until you are released as a witness. I trust everyone has a safe weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 18th day of April, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.40 p.m.,
